Primary Function of Position:
The U.K. ION® Endoluminal Territory Associate reports to the ION® Endoluminal Program Manager (EPM). The ION® Endoluminal Territory Associate plays a critical role in the early adoption of the Ion® platform in expanding access to minimally invasive care for lung biopsy. This individual will be primarily focused on supporting early sustainable users and programs and the development of KOL’s and programs that can highlight the early clinical, economic, and strategic value of ION®.

• Provide procedural support to new users to promote safety and effective progression through their learning curves.

• Work alongside ESR’s to collaborate with senior hospital staff and key physicians in the development and execution of a plan to effectively integrate Ion® at new and existing accounts, ensuring ongoing commitment to and utilization of the system.
• Facilitate critical user and procedural data capture to create effective QTI and benchmarking metrics.
• Collaboration with daVinci local sales teams to ensure consistent alignment and communication with internal and external stakeholders.
• Responsibly manage administrative tasks, SFDC management, submission of expense reports, etc.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Experience:
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.
• A minimum of 1 year sales experience or clinical experience
• Demonstrated ability to manage complexity and work in an environment of change.
• Effective communication and interpersonal skills
• Ability to excel in a high-energy, fast-paced environment.
• Up to 70% travel and/or presence in the field, depending on business needs
• Knowledge of the Pulmonology/Bronchoscopy space environment is a plus.
• Fluent in English and local language required

who are nationals from countries currently on embargo or sanctions status.

About This Job
About the Role
The UK water sector is entering a period of unprecedented investment and transformation. As Egis accelerates the growth of its Water Business in the UK, we are building a high-performing Process Engineering team to help shape this next chapter.
We are inviting applicants who want to play a meaningful role in delivering major water and wastewater programmes in the UK municipal and industrial sectors. Working within a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, you will contribute to technically robust, sustainable and innovative treatment solutions across nationally significant projects.
This is a rare opportunity to join at a key stage of our UK growth journey, helping to establish, shape and expand a process engineering capability built on Egis’ global infrastructure expertise and long-term commitment to the sector.
Key Responsibilities
• Lead process design delivery on multidisciplinary water/wastewater treatment projects across the full design lifecycle.
• Act as process technical lead on projects, owning design strategy, treatment process selection, key decisions, interfaces, risks and quality of deliverables.
• Review and approve process calculations, mass balances, PFDs, P&IDs, basis of design reports, specifications, technical notes, models and supplier/contractor submissions.
• Lead process modelling and simulation activities using tools such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent packages.
• Lead optioneering, process capacity assessments, value engineering, design reviews, HAZOP/SWIFT, commissioning strategy and performance testing input.
• Drive multidisciplinary coordination across Mechanical, EICA, civil/structural, architectural, MEP, construction, commissioning and operations teams.
• Promote lean and digitally enabled delivery through standardised tools, process models, automation, data analysis and reusable templates.
• Provide technical assurance and support project managers with technical risk, scope, resourcing, programme and change control.
• Mentor and manage engineers where appropriate, supporting recruitment, development and chartership progression.
• Contribute to bids, client engagement, opportunity shaping and growth of the process capability.

Qualifications
Minimum Requirements
• BEng/MEng or equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering or closely related discipline.
• Chartered Engineer or Incorporated Engineer status with a relevant professional institution, such as IChemE.
• Typically 8–10+ years’ relevant process design experience.
• Background must be from water, wastewater and/or biosolids/sludge treatment design.
• Proven ability to act as process discipline lead or senior technical lead on multidisciplinary projects.
• Strong technical expertise in water/wastewater treatment process design, including process selection, mass balance, process capacity, PFDs, P&IDs and design basis development.
• Practical experience using process modelling/simulation packages such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent.
• Strong understanding of UK water industry standards, CDM 2015, process safety, safety-by-design, regulatory drivers and common delivery models.
• Confident client-facing communicator with experience leading workshops, technical reviews and design discussions.
• Experience mentoring or managing engineers and supporting technical capability development.
Desirable Skills / Knowledge
• Deep experience in wastewater treatment, clean water treatment, sludge/bioresources, nutrient removal, water reuse/recycling, process optimisation, chemical dosing, energy recovery or low-carbon design.
• Experience delivering AMP8, WINEP, SRO, D&B, framework, alliance or contractor-led projects.
• Advanced capability in BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu, process model calibration, scenario testing, dynamic simulation or operational optimisation.
• Experience developing process design standards, calculation tools, modelling workflows, QA processes or reusable digital templates.
• Experience contributing to recruitment, resource planning, bid writing, technical proposals, client presentations or new service development.
Please note that you must have the right to work in the UK to be considered for this position.

Additional Information
What’s in It for You?
• An exciting new growth role in a fast‑organic growing UK business, offering clear and accelerated career progression
• Top Employers 2025 - Egis recognised across four continents for excellence in HR practices, having been awarded the prestigious Top Employer 2025 certification. Top Employers Institute is the global authority on recognising excellence in people practices.
• A global leader in green infrastructure - we’re proud to lead the way in sustainable infrastructure, mobility and energy, innovating across the entire value chain and every aspect of the built environment.

• Hybrid and flexible working

About This Job
About the Role
The wind tunnel and CFD tell us what the car should do. The track tells us what it actually does. As our Senior Trackside Aerodynamicist, you are the person who works out the difference. You will be responsible for the aerodynamic performance of the car at the circuit, turning track data into clear aerodynamic understanding and getting it to race engineering fast enough to shape setup decisions while the session is still running.
You will be part of the trackside engineering team and act as the principal link between the Aero Development Race teams. That means owning the quality and interpretation of trackside aero analysis, checking that surfaces, fit, sealing and configuration match specification, and working with the build team to resolve anything that does not. It also means making sure that what we learn at the track goes back into the development programme, so every race weekend makes the next car better. Expect to explain complex aero to engineers and drivers in plain language, often against a ticking clock.
As part of this role, regular travel and race attendance is required.
Key Responsibilities include:
• Owning trackside aerodynamic analysis across all race and test sessions, delivering conclusions within the running schedule
• Interpreting and presenting aero data to engineers and drivers to inform setup decisions and development direction
• Identifying aerodynamic limitations and quantify the lap time cost of each
• Briefing the race team on development items ahead of each event, including the expected gain and how it will be measured
• Improving track-to-tunnel and track-to-CFD correlation, and specify the instrumentation and on-track experiments needed to validate development items
• Developing trackside analysis tools and methodology, and define best practice for the group
• Acting as the point of reference for trackside aerodynamics, working with development aerodynamics, vehicle performance and race engineering to reach agreed conclusions
About You
You are someone who can take a large, noisy dataset and pull out a clear conclusion, then present it clearly and with the right level of confidence. You understand the trade-offs between aerodynamic, mechanical and tyre optima, and you know when a compromise on aero is the right call. You stay calm when the clock is running, and you can make a defensible decision and be honest about the residual risk. You build good relationships easily, whether you are talking to a driver, a race engineer or a designer back at the factory.
What we are looking for:
• A degree in aerodynamics, aeronautical or mechanical engineering, or a closely related discipline (equivalent demonstrable experience is welcome)
• Demonstrable experience in a race car aerodynamics or performance engineering role
• Previous experience in Formula 1 or another elite motorsport category
• Strong working knowledge of full-scale race car data acquisition hardware and software, and their limitations
• Proven data analysis capability in MATLAB, Python or similar, including building and maintaining your own analysis tools
• Willingness and ability to travel internationally throughout the race and test calendar

Additional Information

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/shawbrook/74400.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The Customer and Accounts platforms are the spine of the Core Banking Platform. The Customer Platform holds the Bank’s single, deduplicated view of every person and organisation we deal with. The Accounts Platform is the layer every system in the Bank goes through to create and service accounts on Thought Machine Vault Core. Every other platform, franchise and squad depends on both.
This role owns the product agenda across the two. You will run a single roadmap, own the API contracts other teams build against, and define how these platforms behave to the level of precision an engineer can build from: how a customer is matched, merged and maintained, how accounts are created and move through their lifecycle, how instructions and events flow to and from Vault Core, and what happens at every boundary and edge case in between.
It is a deliberately deep, hands-on platform role for someone who is energised rather than daunted by data models, API versioning, idempotency and failure modes, and who is comfortable that their users are other engineering teams rather than end customers.
Roadmap & Initiative Definition
• Own a single product roadmap across the Customer and Accounts platforms, sequenced against franchise commercial priorities, Core Banking Programme commitments and the platform’s delivery capacity.
• Balance platform reliability, new capability and migration work in one plan, and make the trade-offs between them explicit rather than letting the loudest demand set the order.
• Run discovery with the squads and franchises that depend on the platform, establishing the underlying customer and business need, the platform behaviour it implies, and whether the platform can support it.
• Convert consumer demand into well-formed initiatives with a clear problem statement, scope, dependencies and definition of success, so the squad has a credible, prioritised pipeline of work.
• Take on the problems that are too large or too cross-cutting for any single product squad to own, the ones that only become solvable when one platform holds the whole picture.
• Own migration and decommissioning planning for legacy customer and account infrastructure, including how records are matched, moved, reconciled and proven correct.
• Bring a point of view. Where a request is poorly formed, unaffordable or better solved elsewhere in the estate, say so early and propose the alternative.
Product Definition on the Platform
• Own how the Customer Platform behaves — matching, merge and deduplication rules, what constitutes the golden record, how customer data is maintained and corrected, and the downstream consequences of any change to that record — including configuration and the rationale behind every parameter choice.
• Own how the Accounts Platform behaves — account creation, lifecycle states and closure, how instructions reach Vault Core, and how posting and event behaviour is exposed back to consuming systems.
• Treat the platform API surface as a product in its own right: own its definition, versioning and documentation, so every consuming system has stable contracts to build against and no consumer is surprised by a change.
• Set the standards for how other squads integrate with the platform, covering integration patterns, idempotency, error handling and testing, and make sure they are understood and followed.
• Translate consumer needs, regulatory obligations and platform constraints into unambiguous requirements, with user stories and acceptance criteria covering happy path, unhappy path, boundary and invalid-input cases.
• Decide whether a need is met by configuration, new platform capability, or a change in the consuming system, and make the trade-off explicit rather than defaulting to build.
• Build in the controls the Bank needs from the outset: FCA and Consumer Duty outcomes, accuracy and lineage of customer and account data, auditable behaviour, and correct treatment under financial crime and data protection obligations.
• Grow the Customer Platform as the Bank’s single source of truth for who we deal with, rather than one more system holding a partial view.
• Make each new product and franchise faster and lower-effort to launch by building reusable capability rather than one-off integrations.
• Review implemented behaviour against requirements alongside engineers, and own product sign-off through test and UAT.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work day to day with the engineers on the platform squad, not just their leadership, in refinement, in design discussions and in defect triage. The quality of this working relationship is the single biggest determinant of success in the role.
• Partner with the franchise and product squads that consume the platform, and hold the line on platform integrity under delivery pressure, balancing franchise urgency against consistent, scalable foundations.
• Work with Operations to understand how customers and accounts are actually onboarded and serviced, and bring that reality into platform decisions.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/asos/7440001540.description_excerpt:
About This Job
About The Role
ASOS is looking for a Brand Planning Manager to join the Brand & Planning Marketing team. This is a planning role responsible for leading, translating brand and business strategy into one integrated, prioritised and executable global brand plan.
The role sits at the handover point between strategy and execution. It will connect Brand Strategy, Brand Marketing, Brand Heat, Product, Commercial, Performance Marketing, Creative, channel teams, agencies and local markets, turning strategic direction into clear annual and seasonal plans, market-ready calendars, channel roles, investment principles and measurable outcomes.
Working closely with the Global Brand & Planning Marketing Lead, the Brand Planning Manager will own the day-to-day planning rhythm across the year, lead market engagement and the communications model, and create the clarity, governance and decision points needed to move plans forward. The role will not own campaign creative briefing. Its focus is ensuring that strategy is translated into an aligned plan which enables teams to brief, develop and execute effectively.
This role will combine integrated planning leadership, market partnership, cross-functional influence and operational ownership, while providing senior direction and quality assurance across the team’s reporting and effectiveness work so that insight consistently feeds forward into future plans.
Why This Role Matters
The Brand & Planning Marketing team is building a more connected operating system across planning, execution and effectiveness. The Brand Planning Manager will help create the capacity and senior ownership needed for the Global Brand & Planning Marketing Lead to focus primarily on strategic planning, while ensuring reporting remains well governed, decision-oriented and connected to the plan.
The role will act as a planning control tower for Brand Marketing: creating one view of the global and local calendar, clarifying ownership and dependencies, bringing market “Fit to Win” needs into planning, and ensuring agreed plans move confidently from strategic direction into channel and market execution.
What You Will Be Responsible For
1. Integrated Annual & Seasonal Brand Planning
• Maintain the integrated full-year brand plan and four seasonal plans, connecting brand priorities, product and commercial inputs, customer and cultural moments, campaign types, channel roles, markets and investment.
• Translate strategy into clear planning parameters, priorities, phasing, sequencing, success measures and decision points that enable execution teams to develop channel and campaign responses.
• Lead the day-to-day annual and seasonal planning rhythm, including planning forums, inputs, working sessions, readiness reviews, decision logs and senior stakeholder updates.
• Ensure the plan balances long-term brand building with traffic and commercial priorities, with clear roles across Brand Marketing, Volume Collaborations, Brand Heat and Performance Marketing.
• Maintain a single source of truth across planning documents, calendars, milestones, assumptions, ownership and dependencies, surfacing gaps, overlaps and risks early.
• Use performance evidence, customer insight, product priorities, market context and previous learnings to improve future plans and recommendations.
2. Market Planning, Calendars & “Fit to Win”
• Act as the day-to-day Brand Planning point of contact for local market marketing teams, building a consistent two-way planning rhythm between central and local teams.
• Own the global market marketing calendar, bringing together global campaigns, locally relevant moments, product availability, adaptable assets, media support, market-led activations and key dependencies.
• Lead the process to understand each priority market’s “Fit to Win”: the customer, commercial, cultural, media and executional needs required for activity to succeed locally.
• Ensure market needs are considered early enough to shape the central plan, rather than being managed only at handover, while maintaining clear global priorities and guardrails.
• Drive bilateral alignment on where markets will amplify global activity, where localisation is required, where locally led activity is more appropriate, and what support, ownership and funding are needed.
• Create clear market handovers and participation views, escalating unresolved trade-offs and ensuring final decisions are reflected in one integrated global plan.
3. Communications Model & Channel Integration
• Drive the ASOS communications model, translating brand objectives and audience priorities into clear roles for paid, owned and earned channels across campaigns and always-on activity.
• Partner with Brand Strategy, Consumer Insight, Performance Marketing, Media, Social, PR, Talent, CRM, Homepage/App, Search and other channel teams to define how channels work together across the customer journey.
• Establish practical planning principles for channel role, audience, message, format, timing, sequencing, weighting and investment, ensuring these are applied consistently in annual and seasonal plans.
• Use effectiveness evidence and channel learnings to evolve the communications model, resolve duplication or gaps, and strengthen the connection between reach, consideration, traffic and commercial outcomes.
• Drive adoption of the model through clear tools, playbooks, forums and governance, ensuring it becomes a working planning framework rather than a standalone strategy document.
4. Strategy-to-Execution Handover & GTM Governance
• Own the planning handover from strategic direction into executable GTM plans, making sure teams understand the objective, role of the moment, audience, market implications, channel parameters, investment guardrails and measures of success.
• Partner with Brand Project Management and execution leads to translate the integrated plan into workstreams, critical paths, owners, milestones and dependencies without taking ownership of campaign creative briefing.

Our Ground Engineering team in the United Kingdom and Ireland (UK&I) comprises 150 professionals who provide a comprehensive range of services, including project management, feasibility studies, ground investigation design and interpretation, detailed design, contract administration, and construction supervision. We work on ground engineering projects across the UK&I and internationally, supporting both internal and external clients. Our primary focus areas include energy, water, nuclear (decommissioning and new build), power, road and rail, aviation, ports and harbours, as well as commercial and industrial developments, and landslip investigation and remediation.
We work for leading UK and International clients, including National Grid, BP, Sellafield, Associated British Ports, Transport Scotland, National Highways, Transport Infrastructure Ireland, Network Rail, and local authorities, as well as for prominent contractors and developers. Our impressive portfolio features a range of regional and national projects, such as the Great Grid Upgrade, STEP Fusion,  pumped storage hydro projects in the Scottish Highlands, Snowdonia VIP, A83 Rest and be Thankful, M54-M6 Link Road, water schemes for various water utilities clients (UK&I) and HMNB Devonport redevelopment. Additionally, we are involved in overseas projects such as Eastlink in Sweden.
As a Ground Engineering Apprentice, you will work alongside experienced geotechnical engineers and engineering geologists whilst studying towards a Level 6 Degree Apprenticeship in either Civil Engineering or Geoscience. You will gain practical experience across a variety of ground engineering projects, developing the technical knowledge necessary to build a successful career within the industry.

• Assist with desk studies and site investigations.

• Help analyse geological and geotechnical data.

• Develop your technical and professional skills through a structured apprenticeship programme.

• Ability to work effectively within a team.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/gdmsi/744000146.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Join a team developing the next generation of mission computing technology for advanced military aircraft, taking technical ownership of processor platforms that will underpin multiple future defence programmes. This role offers the opportunity to influence product strategy, architecture and technology direction across a portfolio of cutting-edge airborne systems.
As a Senior Systems Engineer within the Core Technologies team at GD-MS UK, you will lead the development and evolution of our common processor-based VPX card portfolio, which supports a wide range of defence programmes and customers. You will provide technical leadership, drive innovation and ensure these foundational platform components deliver the performance, reliability and scalability required for demanding operational environments.
A key aspect of the role will be championing the adoption of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), applying model-based approaches to new product developments while guiding the transition of existing processor card product lines. You will oversee the integration of MBSE practices alongside traditional documentation methods, ensuring continuity, compliance and traceability throughout this transformation.
Key Responsibilities
• Establish and build comprehensive SysMLv2 requirements models for new processor-based card developments from inception, ensuring consistency and traceability across all system elements - Conduct comprehensive systems-level analysis and technical evaluations to identify optimisation opportunities and resolve complex engineering challenges such as FPGA integration, utilising both traditional and model-based approaches
• Own the Verification & Validation (V&V) cycle, ensuring testing is comprehensively planned and delivered to achieve full sign-off of product design, with complete traceability to requirements models maintained throughout the development lifecycle
• Collaborate with mechanical, hardware, firmware, and software engineering teams to ensure seamless integration and system compatibility across all project deliverables, promoting adoption of MBSE practices across disciplines
• Lead technical design reviews and provide expert guidance to junior engineers on both traditional systems engineering and model-based systems engineering methodologies, fostering knowledge sharing and continuous improvement - Develop and maintain detailed technical documentation, including design specifications, architecture diagrams, and SysMLv2 models, ensuring alignment between document-based and model-based representations
• Ensure all processor-based card designs comply with relevant industry standards, regulatory requirements, and organisational quality standards for defence applications - Analyse emerging technologies and industry trends to inform future Digital IO card development strategies and systems engineering practices

Qualifications
Required Skills & Experience
• Proven experience in systems engineering with a focus on processor or hardware design
• Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with meticulous attention to detail
• Knowledge of processor architectures and system-level design principles
• Excellent technical documentation and communication skills
• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary engineering teams
Desirable Skills & Experience
• Experience with hardware validation, testing methodologies, and performance analysis
• Familiarity with CAD tools, simulation software, and technical modelling platforms
• Leadership or mentoring experience within technical engineering environments
• Familiarity with semiconductor design processes and processor card manufacturing
• Knowledge of industry standards such as PCIe, DDR, and other relevant specifications
• Experience with power management, thermal analysis, and signal integrity considerations
• Background in systems architecture and platform-level design
• Understanding of design for manufacturability (DFM) and cost optimisation principles
• Experience working with or familiarity with AI/ML models is preferred

Additional Information
This role has a salary of between £50,000 and £60,000 plus our flexible benefits package.
We are open to this role being spent with time working from home and in the office (hybrid - typically 3 days working in office) on a weekly basis or fully in our offices.
We pride ourselves in being a great place to work with a shared sense of purpose, offering impressive benefits:
• A compressed nine-day fortnight and compressed hours - which means every other Friday off.
• A personalized career development plan, alongside regular progress reviews - supporting and valuing your progression within the Company.
• A flexible working environment where your contributions are recognized and rewarded with flexible benefits
We believe in maintaining a diverse workplace - inclusive of beliefs, cultural background, job experiences, thoughts and ideas. If who we are and what we do resonates with you, we welcome you to join our inclusive team!
Our success is fuelled by our colleagues and the wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills they bring to the Company.
We are a Disability Confident Employer, as such we offer an interview to disabled people who meet the minimum criteria for the job.
Please email disabilityconfident@gd-ms.uk if you would like your application to be considered under the DC Scheme.
All successful/appointed applicants must be able to obtain a level of UK Security clearance that is appropriate for the role and undertake suitable Right to work checks.
Every application matters to us. We want you to know that each application we receive is reviewed by a real person—not just an algorithm. Our screening questions are also carefully considered to help us understand your experience and fit for the role.
We appreciate the time you take to apply.

About This Job
For Universal United Kingdom Resort (UUKR), the Site Planning Compliance Manager is a fully site-based role (5 days a week) embedded within the live construction environment, responsible for overseeing contractor activities and ensuring planning requirements are understood, implemented, and maintained across the Entertainment Resort Complex (ERC).
Working closely with contractors, site managers and delivery teams on a day-to-day basis, the Site Planning Compliance Manager acts as the key on-site interface for planning compliance. The role provides practical oversight of construction activities, undertaking regular site inspections, identifying potential or actual areas of non-compliance, and working directly with contractors to agree and implement corrective actions. A key focus is translating planning permissions, conditions and statutory obligations into clear, workable requirements that can be effectively applied within an active and complex construction program.
The role is responsible for monitoring contractor compliance with requirements including Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs), habitat protection and enhancement measures, flood mitigation conditions, working hour restrictions, approved methodologies, and all applicable Special Development Order (SDO) conditions. The Site Planning Compliance Manager works proactively with contractors, consultants and internal teams to ensure these obligations are consistently embedded within site operations.
Alongside day-to-day contractor management and site oversight, the role supports the preparation, review and coordination of planning compliance documentation, bringing practical construction insight to contractor submissions and proposed methodologies. The Site Planning Compliance Manager also plays a key role in preparing for and facilitating site visits by governmental, planning and regulatory bodies, ensuring the site is ready and that compliance requirements can be clearly demonstrated.
Through regular engagement with contractors and site teams, the Site Planning Compliance Manager will foster a strong culture of planning compliance, ensuring obligations are clearly communicated, understood and consistently implemented throughout all phases of construction.

• Ensure site readiness and accurate representation of compliance status.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Construction Management, Environmental Management, Planning, Engineering, or a related field is preferred.
• Significant experience in construction site-based roles with strong understanding of live construction environments and contractor operations.
• Proven experience in planning compliance, planning conditions, or environmental management within major construction or infrastructure projects.
• Strong working knowledge of planning permissions, CEMPs, environmental constraints, and regulatory compliance requirements.
• Ability to interpret planning and environmental requirements and translate them into practical, buildable site solutions.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels from site operatives to senior stakeholders.

About This Job
Purpose of Role:
Lead the continuous development of Environment, Health and Safety management systems and culture that meet regulatory requirements, drive everyday adoption of safe working practices by all stakeholders and are relevant to the activities of the business.
Input to and oversee the implementation of the company’s Health & Safety strategy and the Environmental strategy in line with ISO14001.  Develop, review, update and drive the annual improvement plan to align with the Thermal strategic business plan, improve risk management and company performance, and strengthen employee engagement and wellbeing.
Be the company’s EH&S subject matter expert and key contact for Senior Group Health, Safety and Environment ensuring local strategy and activities are aligned with Group expectations, sharing best practice across Senior Group sites.
Provide line management, leadership and development for the EH&S Officer, role modelling our Values and Behaviours.
Key Responsibilities:
• Review, update and implement the EH&S strategy and annual objectives in support of the business plan. Provide oversight, prioritisation and reporting on progress, risks and performance to the General Manager and Senior Leadership Team (SLT).
• Develop, maintain and communicate EH&S performance metrics to report on progress and trend analysis.
• Provide weekly plant updates for the General Manager.
• Attend monthly Health & Safety meetings led by the EH&S Officer, as a Senior stakeholder.
• Liaise with all external agencies and bodies, including enforcing authorities, insurance companies and trade organisations.

• Review and maintain the Business Continuity Plans including all emergency arrangements related to fire, first aid and chemical spill situations.

Essential
• Good all-round knowledge of Environmental, Health & Safety legislation, including the ability to read and interpret Acts of Parliament, Regulations, Approved Codes of Practice and Guidance notes.
• Experience of working within an Environmental, Health and Safety role in a manufacturing environment
• Day-to-day management of risk assessments and their application in a manufacturing environment to drive a Safety-first culture.
• Working knowledge of Environment, Health & Safety standards such as ISO14001, their implementation and retention through successful audits.
• Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the confidence and ability to present to different stakeholder groups e.g. colleagues, leadership, customers, external agencies.
• Resource management experience including budget and cost management and identifying efficiencies.
• Organisation skills with the ability to prioritise and make data driven decisions with minimal supervision
• Ability to influence and engage others when needed, to promote action and implement lasting change.
• Results focused with excellent attention to detail.
• NEBOSH General Certificate in Occupational Safety and Health
Desirable
• Experience of working within an Environmental, Health and Safety role in a manufacturing environment in the Aerospace sector
• Experience of Nadcap processes: Heat Treatment, Chemical Processing, Welding, NDT, and Non-Conventional Machining and their EH&S requirements.
• NEBOSH Diploma
• Manual Handling Trainer/ DSE Assessor
• Knowledge of solvent regulations and associated extraction requirements

About This Job
We are looking for an experienced Senior Service Designer to work within a multidisciplinary team delivering complex digital services for a UK public sector client.
You will lead service design activity across the service lifecycle, working from Discovery and Alpha through Beta and Live, depending on the assignment. You will help teams understand complex service landscapes, identify user and organisational needs, and design coherent end-to-end services across digital and non-digital channels.
Working alongside user researchers, interaction designers, content designers, product managers, business analysts, delivery managers, developers, architects, policy colleagues and operational teams, you will ensure services are designed around user needs while considering policy, technology and operational constraints.
You will be expected to work confidently within a GOV.UK Service Standard and Government Digital and Data environment, helping teams make evidence-based design decisions and prepare services for assessment where required.
Key responsibilities
You will:
• Lead service design activity within an Agile multidisciplinary delivery team.
• Map as-is and to-be services, identifying pain points, dependencies, opportunities and gaps across the end-to-end journey.
• Create and maintain service blueprints, journey maps, service maps, ecosystem maps and other appropriate service-design artefacts.
• Understand the relationship between user-facing journeys and the processes, people, policy, data and technology that support them.
• Translate user research, analytics, operational insight and wider evidence into actionable service improvements.
• Work closely with user researchers to ensure service decisions are grounded in a strong understanding of user needs.
• Collaborate with interaction and content designers to create coherent experiences across digital and non-digital touchpoints.
• Work with product, business analysis, architecture, technology, policy and operational colleagues to understand constraints and design viable services.
• Plan and facilitate workshops, co-design sessions, service-mapping activities and collaborative decision-making.
• Prototype service concepts and test assumptions early, iterating designs based on evidence and feedback.
• Identify dependencies and systemic issues that may affect the successful delivery of the service.
• Communicate complex service journeys and design decisions clearly to senior stakeholders and multidisciplinary teams.
• Build consensus around service-design approaches while constructively challenging assumptions where necessary.
• Contribute to Service Standard assessments and assurance activity where required.
• Champion accessibility, inclusion and user-centred design throughout delivery.

Qualifications
We are particularly interested in contractors who can demonstrate:
• Strong experience as a Senior Service Designer within UK central government, wider public sector or another GDS-aligned environment.
• Practical experience designing services in line with the GOV.UK Service Standard and user-centred design principles.
• Experience working across one or more government delivery phases such as Discovery, Alpha, Beta or Live.
• Evidence of designing complex services end-to-end, and across multiple channels.
• Strong service mapping and visualisation skills, including service blueprints, user journeys and ecosystem/service maps.
• Experience translating user research and other evidence into service-design decisions.
• Strong workshop facilitation and co-design skills.
• Experience working with a broad range of stakeholders, including senior stakeholders, policy, operational and technical colleagues.
• Ability to navigate ambiguity, bring structure to complex problems and establish a clear service-design direction.
• Strong understanding of accessibility and inclusive design, including designing for users with different access needs.
• Ability to communicate and defend design decisions using clear evidence.
• Experience identifying measures or success criteria that can be used to understand service performance and impact.
• Experience using collaborative design and mapping tools such as Miro, Lucid or equivalent, with an understanding of Figma or similar prototyping tools.
• Experience preparing for or contributing to GOV.UK Service Standard assessments.
• Experience working on services involving complex policy, operational, data or technology dependencies.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/catch22/7440001.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Who we are
Catch22 exists to help build a society where everyone has a good place to live, good people around them, and a fulfilling purpose. We call these our '3Ps'.
We achieve this in two ways. First we improve lives on the frontline through delivery of public services. Secondly, we use our knowledge to change 'the system', to fix the complex web that can trap and disempower those it was set up to help. With the heart of a charity and the mindset of a business, we are uniquely placed to deliver on this challenging agenda.
About Catch22’s Education hub
Catch22 provides young people aged 4 to 18 with alternative and special education in order for them to progress and succeed in sustained education or employment. We do this through high quality teaching and learning based on effective relationships that enable the achievement of life skills and meaningful qualifications.
Where you fit in
As Key Worker at Include Norfolk you will manage, support and develop a group of young people and their families. This will be achieved by building trusting relationships using individual sessions, group work, family visits and other interventions such as, reading interventions, writing interventions and targeted support groups. You’ll oversee a holistic person-centred approach to a young person’s journey from entry to exit, bridging the gap between their academic, behavioural and therapeutic needs, whilst simultaneously preparing them for post-16.
The Key Worker will develop individual pupil support plans that brings together internal, external and multi-agency professionals in order to support development, attainment and progression.
Main Duties & Accountabilities
Service Users
• Work with the Assistant Head Teachers and Pastoral Leads to develop a case load and support students to engage within the school environment by providing initial assessment of learners’ educational, emotional and behavioural needs and tailor advocacy and support programs around these.
• Work with colleagues to design, implement and review pupil support plans for each young person in the caseload according to identified needs at assessment. Specific consideration should be given to establishing critical baseline data regarding attendance, attainment and predicted grades followed by the use of agreed performance monitoring methodology relating to soft and hard outcomes.
• To drive attendance within your caseload, this includes making attendance calls (daily), attending attendance meetings where necessary, and running attendance interventions, as agreed by the Attendance Support Officer & Pastoral Manager.
• To work closely with teaching staff to ensure continuity of delivery and concretisation of learning lessons whether they be educational or social.
• To organise and deliver 1:1 and small group targeted support, advice, guidance, practical help and mentoring for learners as appropriate to their needs and context.
• To ensure all young people in the caseload are risk assessed regularly to identify issues and concerns relating to vulnerability and risk of harm to self or others. This includes any attendance risk assessments.
• To track pastoral progress of the young people in your caseload with regards to school attainment, classroom behaviour and risk of exclusion in order to inform development and review of intervention content.
• Under the guidance of the Pastoral Site Lead or Assistant Headteacher liaise with, and make referrals to, other agencies where necessary.
• Participate in multi-disciplinary teams and meetings, for example PEPs, planning and review, core group.
• Willingness to work in a range of settings including school, college, court, police station and young offender’s institutions. Working in a flexible manner to include occasion evening and residential trips.
• Ensure Pupil support plans are up to date regularly, reflecting their daily support needs.
• To ensure all safeguarding concerns are recorded timely and accurately (same day) in line with the safeguarding policy.
• To ensure all behaviours within school are managed effectively and timely inline with the behaviour policy.
For Resources
• Keep accurate records, which might be used in case conferences and regular professional meetings.
• To efficiently record all details of each contact or work session with young people using the agreed database system, to keep that data management system up to date and to produce reports to support case reviews and evaluations as requested.
• Ensure the effective and efficient management and organisation of learning and patoral resources, including digital technologies.
• Ensure that all resources have been properly risk assessed and are appropriate for use by pupils with emotional and behavioural difficulties.
Inclusion
• Actively contribute to our ambition of creating an inclusive culture, recognising and embracing difference. Act in line with, promote and carry out all responsibilities with full regard to Catch22’s Equality and Diversity Policy.
• Promote and demonstrate anti discriminatory practice.
Health, Safety and Wellbeing
• Follow safe systems of work at all times in accordance with your responsibilities as an employee of Catch22. Report incidents in line with Catch22’s Health and Safety policy, so that remedial action can be taken to prevent an accident or ill health. Take reasonable care of your own health, safety and wellbeing and help support those around you with theirs.
Other requirements
• Reflect the vision, mission aims and values of Catch22 at all times. Role model Catch22 behaviours.
• Adhere to the schools code of conduct policy, safeguarding policy & behaviour policy at all times.
• Complete mandatory training in line with Catch22’s policy and procedures
This Job Description and Person Specification reflect the duties of the post as they exist at this time and may be subject to change based on the needs of the organisation. The postholder may be required to undertake other duties commensurate with the salary and competence requirements of this post from time to time as required.
What does good look like for this role?
• Improve attitude and engagement of pupils
• Improve attendance and behaviour of pupils
• Provide reports to management of progress by pupil, class and school
• Enable pupils to make academic progress
• Enable pupils to make pastoral and personal progress
• Ensure that you are part of morning and afternoon planning to ensure that you are clear about the expectations for them and the pupils form each lesson
• To participate activity in supervisions and feedback any needs and CPD, as required
• Pupils feel safe within the school environment.
For full job desciption please click here.

Qualifications
• A relevant professional qualification (NVQ level 2) in working with young people, e.g. teaching, youth and community work, social work, counselling, mentoring. Level 2 English and Maths.
• Willingness to complete Teaching Assistant Apprenticeship Level 5,

We have a fantastic new opportunity for a graduate to join the Advanced Targeting line of business as an Optical Engineer. Your role as a Graduate Optical Engineer will be solve real-world engineering challenges, designing and developing mission-critical solutions that power some of the world’s most advanced defence and security systems under the guidance and support of experienced Optical Engineers. The Graduate programme will offer you 18 months of development, with placements in three phases of the product life cycle. You will learn how to use state-of-the-art tools and technology to explore all aspects of the development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, concept design, and design for manufacture, implementation, test, build and product support.
What you’ll do as a Graduate Optical Engineer
As a Graduate Optical Engineer, you will manage your own development towards attaining Optical Engineer level through the Graduate Development Scheme over 18 months.
To achieve this goal, you will be placed in programmes responsible progressing different parts of a product life cycle:
• New product introduction: tasked with learning the core concepts required to increase the manufacturing rate, such as modelling an existing to designs to identify root-cause analysis of observed problems and use of metrology to validate theories.
• Detailed product design: responsible for developing or improving existing designs and supporting the transfer of optical models into a detailed optical and system requirements.
• Novel concepts: to develop technologies both future and improvement of existing products.
Throughout these placements you will learn skills required to communicate technical concepts across a wide array of disciplines. You will be expected support optical procurement and the wider product team in the creation and changing of drawings, tolerancing and how to develop of experiments to prove capability of your designs. Finally, you will be tasked performing technical reviews to assess the limits on technical capability and for creating and conducting optical tests to lower the technical risks of novel EO-Systems and solutions identified as part of wider technological reviews.
What you’ll bring
• A minimum of a 2:1 master’s degree or a higher, such as a EngD or PhD.
• Relevant experience of photonics, such as summer placements, internships or research projects.
• Experience with technical writing and project planning.
• Strong analytical, modelling skills and laboratory skills.
• Evidence of successfully working in a team.
• Enthusiasm for photonics and an interest in developing your technical capabilities.

Our Transaction Advisory Services (TAS) Tax team is structured in a unique way – we are focused on providing the full spectrum of tax services to private equity, across funds, deals and portfolio companies on a wide scope of transactional work both domestically and internationally.
We are leading advisers to mid-market private equity firms and large acquisitive corporates with deal values of anywhere from a few million to over a billion. We support our clients throughout the entire deal lifecycle from the initial proposal stage and assisting with offer terms, undertaking due diligence and advice on the acquisition structure through to completion and post-deal advice.
We work with businesses across a huge range of sectors – from technology and gaming, through to care homes, art galleries, travel and retail. This is a fast-moving and exciting environment. It is technically led but with a keen eye on service and so this role will involve technical tax application, extensive interaction with clients and great interpersonal and organisational skills.
TAS Tax are a small, tight-knit team, and have experienced exceptional growth year on year. We have a strong pipeline and as part of a growing team, you will have significant opportunities to take on responsibility and develop as the team grows.
We are looking for bright and enthusiastic individuals who are looking to step up into a AD role and are interested in a career in M&A tax.

• You will be involved in business development, researching and preparing proposals to win new work and taking part in presentations to prospective clients.
• You will manage project budgets, ensuring bills are raised accurately and promptly, fees are collected in a timely manner and debtors kept to a minimum.
• You will demonstrate an ability to produce a well-supported piece of technical research using legislation, guidance issued by tax authorities and/or the firm’s technical resources.
• You will be responsible for ongoing training and development of your team.

Our leveraged finance lawyers will work on a broad mix of transactions for our clients, including debt financing for public and private M&A, refinancings, recapitalisations and strategic investments. The Leveraged Finance team sits as part of our Finance group within the firm’s Global M&A and Capital (GMAC) practice – alongside M&A, Capital Markets, and Private Capital. o Equipment hierarchy
o Standard jobs
o Job programs
o Scheduling
o Measurements

• Oversight of supplementary maintenance systems from third parties, e.g. oil sample analysis, inspections.

o Equipment
o Standard jobs
o Standard job scheduling (calendar, criteria, and event based)

o Miscellaneous changes (criticality, maintenance strategy,
technical coding)

About the Team
ETF Trading Solutions supports the facilitation of primary market activity, tax-efficient trading strategies and implementation for T. Rowe Price’s ETFs. The team coordinates across Portfolio Management, Trading, ETF Capital Markets, Operations, Tax, Compliance, Investment & Trading Solutions and Technology to ensure ETFs operate efficiently and the platform is structured to scale. The team also develops implementation capabilities that can be leveraged across investment vehicles, including Redemption In Kind (RIK) solutions for mutual funds.
About the Role
The ETF Analyst is an investment implementation and data ownership role within ETF Trading Solutions. The analyst supports pre- and post-trade analysis of Portfolio Manager activity to make full use of the ETF vehicle’s capabilities, while serving as a business owner for the data that enables ETF trading, primary-market activity, portfolio implementation and oversight.
The role requires expertise in ETF mechanics—including creation/redemption activity, basket construction, spreads, premiums/discounts and indicative values—together with a strong understanding of tax lots, tax-lot harvesting and relevant security-level tax considerations. The analyst combines this investment knowledge with quantitative, data engineering and programming skills to develop scalable implementation solutions and improve after-tax and transaction-cost outcomes.
Consistent with the broader Trading Solutions model, data ownership is a core responsibility rather than a downstream support activity. The analyst defines business requirements and data standards, establishes accountability for critical ETF data, monitors quality and controls, prioritizes remediation and enhancement work, and partners with Technology and data-producing/consuming teams to evolve the ETF data model and strategic roadmap. The objective is to create trusted, reusable data foundations that reduce implementation risk, support automation and analytics, and enable the ETF platform to scale.
Principal Responsibilities
ETF Implementation and Investment Solutions
·         Analyze Portfolio Manager trade ideas and portfolio activity to determine efficient implementation methods that leverage the unique capabilities of ETFs.
·         Synthesize security characteristics, liquidity and volatility data, transaction-cost analysis, tax-lot information and input from Portfolio Managers, Traders, ETF Capital Markets Specialists, Portfolio Investment Analysts and Trading Analytics to refine implementation strategies.
·         Support creation/redemption and basket-related analysis, including the evaluation of primary- versus secondary-market implementation and opportunities to improve tax efficiency and reduce transaction costs.
·         Contribute to the development and implementation of tax-efficient trading solutions across investment vehicles, including mutual-fund RIK capabilities.
·         Apply modelling, statistics, optimization and programming to solve investment implementation problems and automate repeatable analytical workflows.
ETF Data Ownership and Governance
·         Act as a business data owner/domain owner for ETF Trading Solutions, with accountability for the fitness, usability and appropriate governance of critical ETF data used in investment and trading workflows.
·         Define and maintain business definitions, data requirements, critical data elements, ownership and stewardship expectations, lineage needs, quality standards and control requirements for ETF data domains.
·         Establish and monitor data-quality measures and controls; investigate exceptions, coordinate root-cause analysis and drive remediation with Technology, Operations, vendors and other data-producing teams.
·         Own the business prioritization of ETF data defects, enhancements and strategic initiatives, balancing investment impact, operational risk, scalability and platform growth.
·         Represent ETF Trading Solutions in data governance forums and ensure business decisions, standards and ownership are clearly documented and communicated.
·         Partner with Technology to develop and evolve the ETF data strategy, target data model, APIs and reusable data services, with clear business acceptance criteria and validation of delivered solutions.
·         Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize and automate data acquisition, transformation, validation and distribution, reducing manual intervention and implementation risk.
·         Ensure new ETF products and capabilities have appropriate data readiness, controls and operating ownership before launch and as they scale.
Analytics, Technology and Platform Development
·         Build and maintain analytical tools and data pipelines supporting ETF implementation, monitoring and decision-making.
Lead the business design and implementation of a scalable ETF reconciliation/data-quality platform, working with our Technology partners to build out the supporting tooling, controls, and exception workflows.
·         Work effectively with APIs, relational databases and structured data formats to extract, transform, validate and integrate data across investment workflows.
·         Use programming and modern development practices to create robust, maintainable solutions, including testing, version control and CI/CD where appropriate.
·         Translate investment and trading requirements into clear specifications for Technology and partner teams, and participate in solution design, testing and implementation.
·         Develop metrics and management information that make data quality, process health, implementation outcomes and platform scalability visible to stakeholders.
Subject Matter Expertise, Communication and Partnership
·         Serve as a subject matter expert on ETF implementation and ETF data, connecting investment, trading, operational and technology…

Job Title:
Business Modernization, Project Manager - Sales & Services
Reporting To:
GVP - Finance
Work Schedule:
Onsite – Buffalo, NY
The Business Modernization Program Project Manager is responsible for planning and delivering assigned ERP modernization workstreams or releases, ensuring scope, schedule, resources, risks, and dependencies are actively managed throughout the implementation lifecycle. This role will partner closely with the Business Process Champion and Data Lead for Sales & Service to drive disciplined project-level execution while ensuring alignment with overall program objectives, milestones, and governance.
This role coordinates cross-functional teams including business stakeholders, IT, system integrators, and third-party partners. The Project Manager ensures transparency, predictability, and delivers rigor, proactively identifying and mitigating risks to support successful adoption, go-live, and stabilization outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Project Planning & Execution
•
Develop and manage detailed project plans aligned to the integrated modernization program schedule, milestones, and governance model.
•
Lead assigned ERP modernization projects or workstreams through all delivery phases: Prepare, Explore, Realize, Deploy, and Hypercare.
•
Manage day-to-day project execution, including task tracking, milestone achievement, and issue resolution.
Scope, Risk & Dependency Management
•
Actively manage project scope, ensuring alignment with approved designs and adherence to formal change control processes.
•
Identify, assess, and manage project-level risks, issues, and dependencies; escalate to the Modernization Program Manager with clear mitigation recommendations.
•
Coordinate cross-workstream dependencies with peer Project Leads to ensure integrated delivery.
Resource & Stakeholder Coordination
•
Coordinate business, IT, system integrator, and third-party resources to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
•
Facilitate effective collaboration across functional and technical teams.
•
Partner closely with Solution Architecture, Functional Leads, and Organizational Change Management (OCM) to align delivery and adoption activities.
Reporting & Governance
•
Prepare and deliver accurate project status reporting, forecasts, and issue updates in alignment with program reporting standards.
•
Issue and RAID log management for related project area(s)
•
Ensure adherence to established program governance, delivery methodology, and quality standards.
Testing, Cutover & Go-Live Support
•
Support testing cycles, defect resolution, cutover planning, and go-live readiness activities.
•
Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards and achieve business stakeholder acceptance.
•
Support knowledge transfer and transition to sustain and operations teams post go-live.
Required Qualifications
Education
•
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
•
5+ years of project management experience supporting implementations or major modernization initiatives. Experience in ERP implementations is preferred.
Skills & Experience
•
Demonstrated experience managing ERP projects or significant ERP workstreams across multiple implementation phases.
•
Strong understanding of ERP implementation lifecycles and structured delivery methodologies (e.g., SAP Activate or equivalent).
•
Proven ability to manage schedules, scope, risks, issues, and dependencies in complex project environments.
•
Experience working with system integrators and coordinating internal and external delivery teams.
•
Strong communication skills with the ability to engage both business and technical stakeholders.
•
Proficiency with project management and reporting tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar).
•
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
•
Ability to operate effectively within a structured program and governance-driven environment.
How We Care For You:
•
Financial Rewards: great compensation package, bonus opportunities, matching 401k, and the ability to participate in Employee Stock Purchase Plan (select locations), Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts
•
Work/Life Balance: Flexible paid time off, holidays and parental leave program, relocation assistance.
•
Health & Welfare: Comprehensive insurance coverage including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, Employee Assistance Plan (“EAP”) and other supplemental benefit coverages.
•
Professional Skills Development: Tuition Assistance, mentorship and coaching opportunities, leadership development and other personal growth programs
•
Culture: Warm, respectful, family-like environment driven by our 12 core values. Multiple Employee Resource Groups led by our employees, open and welcoming to all.

At Johnson Controls, we're shaping the future of smart, healthy, and sustainable buildings and mission- critical environments. As a global leader in building technologies and solutions, we help customers achieve operational excellence through innovation, expertise, and collaboration. Silent-Aire delivers world-class mission critical infrastructure solutions for some of the world's largest technology and data centre operators. This role provides the opportunity to work on complex and innovative projects while developing expertise within one of the fastest-growing sectors in the industry.
What you will do
The Commissioning Engineer is responsible for the installation verification, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and handover of electrical and associated mechanical systems on mission critical projects. The role ensures all systems are commissioned safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project specifications, industry standards, client requirements, and company procedures.
As a Commissioning Engineer, you will support project teams across an assigned customer base, taking ownership of commissioning activities, compliance with client requirements, documentation, reporting, and stakeholder engagement. You will contribute to continuous improvement initiatives, maintain strong supplier and customer relationships, and provide technical input throughout project execution.
How you will do it                                      `
• Support project delivery through all phases, from installation and commissioning to client handover.
• Collaborate with engineering, design, and QA/QC teams to understand operational requirements and identify potential improvements.
• Develop and execute commissioning, qualification, and SAT protocols.
• Prepare system impact assessments, qualification documentation, and validation reports.
• Review project documentation for technical accuracy, compliance, and GMP requirements.
• Ensure systems are safe and ready for start-up, testing, and qualification activities.
• Perform installation verification, system start-up, and functional testing.
• Monitor progress, coordinate daily activities, and ensure milestones are achieved.
• Build strong relationships with client teams and site stakeholders to ensure successful delivery across health & safety, quality, commissioning, and handover activities.
What we look for:
• Ability and willingness to travel internationally.
• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in engineering and project-related activities, ideally within manufacturing, construction, or mission-critical environments.
• Technical qualifications in electrical engineering
• Experience within HVAC systems and Data Centre projects is desirable.
• Controls or Building Management Systems (BMS) experience is an advantage.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
• Proactive, results-driven, and solution-oriented mindset.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Physical & Travel Requirements
• Regular travel to project sites throughout the UK and internationally as required.
• Ability to work on active construction sites.
• Ability to work flexible hours to support commissioning and critical project milestones.

Remote role with regular visits to the tour truck location in Reading.
Your office has 18 holes and a Tour Truck.
Every week on the DP World Tour, our staff athletes step onto the first tee trusting that their clubs are exactly right. Behind that confidence is the COBRA PUMA GOLF Tour Team, and we’re looking for someone to join it.
If you can build a club to the exact spec, keep a mobile workshop running like clockwork, and stay calm when a player needs a new shaft an hour before their tee time, this job is for you.
Run the Tour Truck
Our European Tour Truck is the heart of the operation, and it’ll be yours to keep event-ready. You’ll organise it, stock it and keep track of every component, club, shaft and grip.
Build for the best
You’ll build, customise and service COBRA equipment for our contracted athletes and key Sports Marketing personnel. Every club will be built to the player’s exact specification.

You’ll attend DP World Tour, HotelPlanner Tour and Ladies European Tour events, plus amateur and retail events. On site you’ll provide technical support, equipment servicing and hands-on help for players.
Keep product moving
You’ll prepare, dispatch and track shipments to players. You’ll also work with our Operations team to make sure inbound deliveries arrive, are recorded and get processed without a hitch.
Help make moments happen
You’ll support our Tour Operations Manager and Senior Sports Marketing Manager – Golf in planning and delivering Tour activations, VIP events and retail initiatives.

• A real passion for golf and its technical side

• The confidence to think on your feet and solve problems when plans change
• Great communication skills, whether you’re talking to a Tour pro or a courier
• Flexibility to travel across Europe

Working hours

Leadership and supervision

Decisiveness

Salary: Up to £46,000 depending on experience.
Dynamic (hybrid) working: Predominately on-site (Stevenage) due to workload classification and nature of testing.
Security Clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship.
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Security Check (SC).
What we can offer you:
• Company bonus: Up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year)
• Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
• Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime
• Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days
• Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements
• Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments
• Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
The opportunity:
You will join the Hardware In The Loop (HWIL) team who conduct dynamic missile firing simulations, utilising real missile hardware in support of; product development, performance validation and firing trial preparation.
You will have the opportunity to work within a state-of-the-art test and evaluation facility, unique within the UK. The HWIL testing utilises; real missile hardware, a missile performance model, flight motion tables [to pitch/roll/yaw the hardware] and RF / IR target generation systems [to represent target(s)]. This dynamic testing is controlled by a HWIL developed simulation which runs real-time.
This test and evaluation setup allows HWIL to conduct missile testing across many MBDA products in as close to real world scenarios as possible, exercising missile functionalities such as; in-flight performance, target detection, acquisition and homing.
Your job role may vary with the lifecycle of the missile products you are supporting. Your overall aim will be to; integrate, understand and maintain highly complex simulations, and utilise these to perform missile testing and data analysis – all in support of missile product development.
Your main responsibilities will be to:
•             Understand functionality of the missile sub-systems involved in dynamic HWIL testing,
•             Understand interactions between the missile sub-systems and bespoke test equipment,
•             Interact with relevant subject matter experts across MBDA missile product teams,
•             Develop real time software simulations utilising performance models,
•             Conduct hands-on testing with real missile hardware and software,
•             Analyse missile telemetry data to understand performance and produce technical reports.

Job Description:
PM Growth Analytics – Data Scientist, Marketing Measurement & Insights
We are looking for a Data Scientist to join Growth Analytics in a hands-on role focused on understanding the true value of Performance Marketing. You will combine experimentation, modelling, and business analysis to evaluate marketing effectiveness, explain performance, and translate findings into clear recommendations that guide investment decisions.
This role sits at the intersection of measurement, analytics, and business decision-making. It is suited to someone with solid analytical foundations, strong commercial curiosity, and the ambition to grow into a Senior Data Scientist. You will take ownership of defined analytical projects, with support from experienced colleagues on more complex methodological and strategic questions, and build increasing independence and influence.
Your work will span incrementality testing, marketing mix modelling (MMM), and understanding why realised returns differ from predictions. You will work closely with buying teams, analysts, and technical partners to connect evidence across measurement approaches and help assess Performance Marketing alongside the wider marketing mix. A sister team focuses on model training infrastructure and production pipelines; your focus will be on analytical rigour, interpretation, and applying findings to business decisions.
Your Role Within Our Kingdom
• Connect Measurement to Business Value: You will translate analytical findings into practical recommendations on marketing investment, campaign optimisation, and performance expectations. You will work with stakeholders to connect marketing outcomes to player behaviour and revenue, and follow through to understand whether recommendations improve decisions.
• Deliver Marketing Measurement: You will design and analyse incrementality tests and contribute to MMM and other causal analyses, selecting appropriate approaches with guidance where needed. You will own defined projects from the initial business question through analysis, interpretation, and stakeholder readout.
• Explain Business Performance: You will investigate where and why ROI is over- or under-predicted, distinguishing changes in player value, campaign mix, measurement assumptions, and underlying business performance. You will help stakeholders understand whether a gap calls for action, further investigation, or more time to gather evidence.
• Turn Evidence into Decision Frameworks: You will help translate experiment and model outputs into calibration inputs, performance benchmarks, and repeatable analytical tools. You will bring together evidence from incrementality, attribution, and MMM to support planning and evaluate Performance Marketing within the wider marketing mix.
• Bridge Business and Technical Questions: You will work with marketing stakeholders to frame actionable questions and with technical partners to define data and analytical requirements. You will help ensure measurement outputs are interpreted correctly and used effectively in day-to-day decisions.
• Communicate Clearly and Improve Our Approach: You will explain findings, assumptions, and uncertainty to technical and non-technical audiences. You will challenge inconsistencies, identify opportunities to improve existing approaches, and take on broader ownership as your expertise develops.
Skills to Create Thrills
• Education: Degree in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Experience: Hands-on experience in data science, analytics, experimentation, or marketing measurement, with examples of taking an analytical question through to a useful business recommendation.
• Statistical Foundations: A solid understanding of statistical modelling, hypothesis testing, experimentation, and the distinction between correlation and causation. Practical experience with at least one relevant measurement approach and an interest in developing broader expertise.
• Execution: Able to independently deliver well-scoped analytical work, validate results, and manage priorities. Comfortable working through ambiguity while recognising when to seek input or challenge the original question.
• Commercial Mindset: Curious about what drives business performance and able to connect analytical results to investment choices, expected returns, and practical actions.
• Technical Skills: Proficiency in Python or R and SQL, with experience working with complex datasets and producing clear, reproducible analyses.
• Communication: Able to explain complex findings in accessible language, make recommendations supported by evidence, and communicate uncertainty without losing the practical message.
• Judgement and Growth: Thoughtful about assumptions, data quality, and methodological limitations. Receptive to feedback, quick to learn, and ready to develop towards broader project ownership and greater influence over business decisions.
Tasty Bonus Points
• Experience working with media buying teams, growth marketing, or other commercial stakeholders.
• Familiarity with MMM, GeoLift, holdout testing, synthetic controls, or other causal inference methods.
• Experience analysing ROI, lifetime value, forecast accuracy, or the drivers of changes in commercial performance.
• Understanding of advertising measurement challenges, including attribution bias, selection effects, organic cannibalisation, and platform limitations.
• Exposure to measuring brand or traditional marketing alongside digital Performance Marketing.
• Experience turning analysis into repeatable tools or processes used in planning, forecasting, or optimisation.
• Familiarity with BigQuery, Looker, or similar data and analytics platforms.
• Passion for gaming and curiosity about how player behaviour translates into long-term business value.
About King
With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. Job Description
Your AI era starts now
At Lloyds Banking Group, data isn’t just something we store in the cloud. It’s the juice that keeps ideas flowing, decisions sharper, and progress unstoppable.
Our Chief Data & Analytics Office has one mission: weave data, analytics and AI into every decision we make. The goal? Simple. Every choice, everywhere, driven by data.
As a Data Science & AI Graduate, you won’t be on the sidelines watching the algorithms run the show. You’ll be training models, crafting algorithms, deploying scalable solutions, and showing exactly what AI can do in the real world. Whether you’re optimising performance, unlocking insight or making predictions, everything you do will be rooted in data literacy, ethics and genuine business impact.
Two years. Two game-changing rotations
This two-year programme blends office and home working. Across two year-long placements, you’ll see how we use data and AI to crack big-ticket challenges. From detecting fraud and managing credit risk to decoding customer behaviour and building smarter banking tools.
You could become:
• A Data & AI Scientist uncovering insights, making predictions and solving complex problems with machine learning techniques. Always with an ethical and accurate lens.
• A Machine Learning & AI Engineer designing and deploying robust ML systems that bring data science to life through automation, CI/CD, and modern cloud engineering practices.
• Wherever you land, you’ll be working with some of the biggest datasets in the UK — using everything from Spark and statistical methods to domain knowledge and emerging GenAI applications.
The work you could be doing
• Cloud-native AI engineering and large-scale data platforms, leveraging Google Cloud technologies and modern coding practices to design, build and deploy intelligent solutions, helping the Bank innovate rapidly and deliver value at scale.
