• Generative AI, Large Language Models and autonomous agent systems, building next-generation AI applications using foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures and agent frameworks such as Google ADK and LangChain, helping transform how the Bank serves customers and empowers colleagues.
• Data engineering, MLOps and intelligent automation, creating resilient data pipelines, scalable deployment architectures and automated machine learning workflows using contemporary engineering and CI/CD practices, enabling AI solutions to operate reliably across the enterprise.
• AI assurance, evaluation science and model governance, designing rigorous testing, monitoring and validation frameworks for machine learning models and agentic systems, ensuring AI solutions remain robust, trustworthy and aligned to the Bank's strategic objectives.

• Cloud platforms like GCP
• Data Analysis
• Machine learning techniques, both theory and application
• Generative and Agentic AI
• AI Solution design and evaluation techniques
• CI/CD and DevOps

Job Description:
MORE THAN YOU EXPECTED
Grant Thornton UK LLP is part of a global network of independent audit, tax and advisory firms, made up of some 58,000 people in over 135 countries. We're a team of independent thinkers who put quality, inclusion and integrity first. All around the world we bring a different experience to our clients. A better experience. One that delivers the expertise they need in a way that goes beyond. Personal, proactive, and agile. That's Grant Thornton.
NEW GROUND WON’T BREAK ITSELF.
Every day our teams help people in businesses and communities to do what is right and achieve their goals.
The Office of General Counsel is Grant Thornton UK’s legal function, comprising two sub teams – Disputes and Contracts. The Contracts Team works with all of GT’s service lines and business functions to enable growth whilst managing risk across all our commercial relationships. We work closely with our client-facing colleagues to help deliver the best outcomes for our firm and our clients.
We’re happy to talk flexible working and consider reduced hours and job shares, we’ll support you to balance your work and life.
A look into the role
As a Commercial Legal Counsel within our Office of General Counsel, you will:
• draft and negotiate commercial contracts with key clients, including master services agreements and public-sector framework agreements, ensuring risks are identified, considered and mitigated
• draft and negotiate commercial contracts with suppliers, subcontractors and third parties (collaboration, reseller, sponsorship agreements etc.) to support the firm’s growth
• work cross-functionally with the firm’s Quality and Risk teams, client-facing partners and staff on legal issues faced within the firm’s various service lines
• advise on a wide range of other commercial contracting issues, including international contracts, data-sharing agreements, secondment agreements, and software supply contracts
• keep a close eye on the law relating to contracts and professional liability, share knowledge with the team and deliver training to relevant parts of the firm, and help us leverage AI tools for our work
• help protect the firm whilst enabling it to deliver excellent services to our clients.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as a Commercial Legal Counsel, the minimum criteria you’ll need is to be a qualified lawyer with commercial contracting experience. It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
• an understanding of professional services businesses and risk management issues faced by them
• a pragmatic and commercial, solutions-based approach
• a self-starting attitude and the ability to manage conflicting demands
• excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the drafting of contractual terms
• knowledge of adjacent areas of law, such as data protection, intellectual property etc.
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people, we never settle for what is easy, we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone.  Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.
Our open and accessible culture means you’ll interact with leaders who are interested in you and everything you bring to our firm. The things that set you apart, we value them. That’s why we give you the freedom to bring your whole self to work and pursue your passions inside and outside of work.
We’re also committed to supporting you through different life stages, with a range of family friendly and wider leave policies. You can find full details of our reward, benefits and leave policies on our website: Reward and benefits.
Beyond the job
Life is more than work. The things you do, and the people you’re with outside of work matter, that’s why we’re happy to look at flexible working options for all our roles, and we’ll always do our best to keep your work and life in balance.
The impact you can make here will go far beyond your day job. From secondments, to fundraising for local charities, or investing in entrepreneurs in the developing world, you’ll be giving back to society. It’s that drive to do the right thing that runs through our every move, grounded in our firm’s values – purposefully driven, actively curious and candid but kind.
We’re looking for people who want to contribute, spark fresh ideas and go beyond expectations. People who want to be able to proudly do what’s right, for the firm, our clients, our people and themselves. It’s how it should be.

Linklaters is a global law firm, providing legal services in 20 countries and through 30 offices.
Linklaters is a people business. Being best in class in the eyes of our clients means that our people must be exceptional.
We look not only for brilliant minds, but for people who will thrive in our environment: people who love working collaboratively and demonstrate the innovative, efficient, agile, entrepreneurial, and responsible mind-set we aim to bring to every interaction.
Ours is an environment of outperformance. We achieve this not with targets and incentives, but by fostering a positive, supportive, fair, and open atmosphere.
We respect and value difference but insist on inclusivity. We celebrate all aspects of diversity and challenge any form of bias. This is vital to our ability to work as one team, with a common goal.
Your role
• Bring direction and priorities to life: Work with the Strategy Lead and accountable leaders to understand Technology & Data’s agreed direction, priorities, programmes and significant departmental activity. Show why they matter to the firm, its clients and colleagues. Decisions and accountability remain with the relevant owners.
• Make complexity understandable: Develop enough organisational and technical understanding to communicate with accuracy and confidence. Connect different perspectives, spot what is missing or unclear, and take questions to the right person for resolution.
• Plan communication and engagement: Turn the most important activity across Technology & Data into a joined-up forward plan. Work with sponsors and teams to understand what each audience needs, shape the right messages and choose the most effective approach. Maintain a clear rhythm across the year, using feedback and evidence to improve what follows.
• Create clear and effective materials: Bring together contributions and shape them into clear, concise packs, briefings and presentations. Resolve editorial issues and flag substantive gaps before material reaches its audience.
• Bring colleagues together: Work closely with the CTDO, Strategy Lead and leadership team to make town halls and other forums valuable opportunities for colleagues to hear directly from leaders, understand what is happening and ask questions. Coordinate preparation, delivery and follow-up, helping everyone involved contribute at their best.
• Make progress meaningful: Turn approved roadmaps, KPI scorecards and leadership updates into a clear account of outcomes, progress and material risks. Work with accountable owners to make sure the measures and commentary tell a coherent story. Help each audience understand what the information means and what they need to do next.
• Build connection and participation: Create inclusive, two-way engagement across the global Technology & Data community and, where relevant, with colleagues across the firm. Help colleagues understand the direction, take the action needed and share what they are learning.
• Keep delivery moving: Coordinate planned and short-notice activity, making it easy for busy colleagues to contribute and keeping everyone clear on what is needed and when.
About you
• You communicate exceptionally well in writing, in presentations and in person. You know how to make a complex subject clear without stripping out what matters.
• You can work across strategic, programme and operational contexts, adapting the level of detail and communication approach while maintaining a coherent overall narrative.
• You think analytically and see how different parts of an organisation affect one another. You can build a coherent picture from incomplete or conflicting information and spot important gaps.
• You are curious and ask incisive questions. You test assumptions, learn quickly and distinguish the central issue from supporting detail.
• You enjoy working with people who bring different expertise and perspectives. You listen well, earn trust and are comfortable asking constructive questions, including when working with senior colleagues.
• You are genuinely interested in how technology and data can improve the firm. You do not need to arrive as a technical expert, but you will be keen to understand the opportunities, risks and choices involved.
• You are highly organised and dependable. You can keep several priorities moving, coordinate busy contributors and maintain quality when pace increases.
• You may have developed these skills in communications, change, consulting, analysis, technology or somewhere less conventional. We care more about how you think, work with others and make complex subjects useful than the route you took to get here.
• A rigorous analytical, scientific or technical background would be useful, but it is not essential. What matters is how you think, learn and apply new knowledge.
• Experience of Microsoft 365 engagement channels would be useful, but it is not central to the role.

Technical Skills

• Conducting test system FMEA and implement controls to mitigate risks

Job Description
Cboe Europe is seeking an experienced Outsourcing and Third Party Risk Management Lead to support business owners, who hold first-line ownership of how Cboe Europe identifies, assesses, and manages the risks arising from its use of outsourcing, ICT, and other third party providers, as part of a global Infrastructure team You will run and coordinate the third party risk lifecycle in the first line of defence on behalf of business owners – inventory and classification, risk-based due diligence, contracting, ongoing monitoring, exit planning, and regulatory reporting – and lead implementation of the ICT third party requirements of the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) and the FCA’s new operational incident and material third party reporting regime under PS26/2. Working with technology, operations, procurement, legal, compliance, and audit teams, you will strengthen the resilience of trading services used by hundreds of financial services firms across the UK and EU. The role takes an AI-first approach, automating due diligence, register maintenance, evidence gathering, monitoring, and regulatory reporting.
The successful candidate will operate and enhance first-line processes, procedures, and controls relating to outsourced, delegated, and third party arrangements. They will also support senior management in meeting their responsibilities while driving operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across the organisation.
In this role, you will be responsible for:
Maintaining the third party and ICT third party inventory, including:
• Cboe Europe’s outsourcing register and DORA register of information, ensuring ICT services supporting critical or important functions are correctly identified, classified, and recorded.
• The register of material third party arrangements required under FCA PS26/2 and FG26/4, kept submission-ready for return to the FCA.
• Mapping of third parties to the business services, functions, processes, assets, and controls they support, including impact tolerances, RTOs, and RPOs.
• Subcontracting and nth-party chains for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, with concentration, substitutability, and geographic risk recorded.
• Automated data quality, reconciliation, and evidence-gathering controls so register data stays accurate, complete, and examination-ready.
• Strengthening our First Line of Defence (1LOD) through robust procedures and controls aligned to Cboe's Third Party Management Policy, and a culture of continuous improvement
Running first-line third party risk assessment, due diligence, and contracting by:
• Acting as the first point of contact for business owners on third party or outsourcing matters, guiding them through onboarding, including: risk assessment, contract review, and the approval process; approval decisions remain with business owners, subject to second-line sign-off for high-risk vendors.
• Running proportionate, risk-based due diligence across information security, resilience, data protection, financial crime, financial soundness, and concentration risk, coordinating with subject matter experts to form a pragmatic view of third party relationships.

Job Description:
We are looking for a Senior Python Developer to own and grow the software engineering, automation and testing infrastructure within our R&D Engineering division. The role covers end-to-end testing, CI/CD, internal tooling, automation frameworks and engineering quality across our products, platforms and backend infrastructure. Day-to-day is primarily writing Python and building the systems, tools and frameworks that enable our engineering teams to develop, test and release software with confidence. This is a hands-on Software Engineering role, not a manual QA position.
Please note this is a hybrid role with a minimum expectation of being in the office at least 2 times a week.
About the Role
We're looking for a Senior Python Developer to join the R&D Engineering division at Darktrace.
You'll design, build and maintain the software, tooling and infrastructure that support the development and delivery of our products. This includes developing automated test suites, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer tools and automation frameworks that improve engineering efficiency, software quality and release confidence.
What will I be doing:
While testing and automation are important aspects of the role, this is fundamentally a Software Engineering position. You'll write production-grade Python, contribute to shared libraries and engineering tools, and help shape the way our R&D teams build, test and deliver software across different technologies and platforms. In addition you will be responsible but not limited to:
• Designing and implementing automated test solutions across unit, integration, end-to-end and system-level testing,
• Building and maintaining automation tooling, including CI/CD pipelines, test orchestration, infrastructure provisioning and internal developer tools,
• Developing and owning and improve Python-based frameworks, shared libraries and reusable engineering components,
• Working across different technologies, platforms and infrastructure to support reliable software development and delivery,
• Collaborating with engineers across R&D to define testing and automation strategies for new features, products and services,
• Identifying opportunities to improve test coverage, system reliability, engineering efficiency and developer experience, then drive those improvements,
• Contributing to broader software engineering initiatives, including code reviews, architecture discussions, technical documentation and best practices,
• Taking ownership of engineering projects from design and implementation through to deployment, maintenance and continuous improvement.
What Experience Do I Need?
We're looking for someone with strong Python development experience, ideally gained within a SaaS environment, who is confident writing clean, maintainable and well-structured production code. You'll have a deep understanding of the Python ecosystem, its libraries and modern development tooling, alongside strong software engineering fundamentals, in addition you will:
• Have a good understanding of software testing principles and strategy, including the differences between unit, integration and end-to-end testing
• Experience building automation frameworks, developer tooling or internal engineering platforms would be particularly valuable.
• You'll be comfortable working with Linux systems, networking, shell scripting and general infrastructure concepts.
• Experience with Docker, CI/CD systems and infrastructure automation.
Above all, you'll have an engineering mindset towards automation and quality. You see testing infrastructure and developer tooling as software products in their own right, taking ownership of building and improving systems that make engineering teams more efficient.
Nice to Have
It would be beneficial if you also have experience in some of the following areas:
• Working across multiple operating systems or technology platforms,
• A background in cybersecurity, networking, distributed systems or large-scale software infrastructure,
• Familiarity with cloud infrastructure and virtualisation, such as AWS, cloud provisioning or virtual machines,
• Building or maintaining custom test frameworks, automation platforms or developer tooling,
• Contributing to shared or internal Python libraries,
• Working within a large-scale R&D or product engineering environment.
As a growing business strengthening its governance and controls, this role plays a part in supporting high standards of integrity and accountability.

Background:
CME Group runs some of the world’s largest and most important trading venues, including derivatives exchanges, FX/FI platforms. To support our unique data and analytics products, we are now building a unified API-first distribution framework, simplifying consumption and value extraction.
The Role:
We are seeking a key stakeholder for the CMEG External Data-Analytics (DA) APIs and distribution services. This is a high-impact, individual contributor (IC) role for an individual who can navigate complex enterprise systems and deliver a modern, developer-first experience. This customer-facing role serves as the technical link between our APIs and the customer, acting as a high-level practitioner who crafts SDKs and delivery mechanisms to make complex market data easy to consume. You will translate direct customer feedback into refined requirements for the product team while solving integration hurdles firsthand. By bridging these gaps, you will ensure our technical ecosystem is both highly functional and seamless for clients to adopt.
Our API First Vision
• Our external API is the singular point where our strategy, technology, and customer experience converge to create value.
• Our corporate DA strategy focuses on "activation," which involves externalizing proven internal IP and exposing it through a simple, consumable API, as well as adding net-new IP jointly developed with our customers.
• The API is our "single, unified distribution channel". It serves as the "handover point" where internal engineering ends and the customer or partner ecosystem begins.
• The API provides a "single 'front door'" for customers. By using a "unified API”, barriers to consumption are removed, integration time is reduced, development costs lowered, and a consistent experience provided across all data latencies (Real-time, Recent History, and Deep History), data types (time series, metadata, unstructured) and services.
• Internal users are recognized as ultra-valuable sources of feedback. By mandating both internal and external DA workflows through the same SDK, we create a shared experience for both sets of users.

• Public Schema Registry: Implement a publicly accessible registry (e.g., Protobuf, JSON or Avro) that allow internal teams and partners to generate their own client software.
• Developer Collateral
• Simplify Public Messaging: Partner with internal stakeholders to clearly communicate CME Group’s D&A value proposition.
• Technical Documentation: Evaluate,  implement and maintain  an API documentation library and migrate existing fragmented solutions to it.
• Publish Reference Docs: Create first-class, detailed technical reference documentation that serves as the definitive contract for all API behaviour and usage.
• Accelerate Time-to-Value: Develop practical tutorials, code samples, and dashboard templates to empower customers to self-serve and validate products rapidly.
• Data Plane
• Expand Cloud Distribution: Work with our customers and product teams to extend our existing data offerings to meet customer cloud demand. Abstracting cloud specific technologies away and provisioning a common messaging layer.
• Abstraction Layers: Work with our customers to better understand if/how we can improve data delivery for deep history and data sharing services so that accessing large datasets feels identical to a standard, programmatic API call..
• Enforce Schema Consistency: Use a centralized schema registry to ensure identical data models and field names across different services and latency tiers.
• Control Plane
• Normalize Authentication: Work with our central technology team to ensure a unified CMEG credential system that retires legacy approaches and hides cloud-specific complexity from the user.
• Downstream Distribution Technologies: Support external facing distribution technologies to provision products, including Bobsled, SFTP, Curl, email, etc.
• Implement Group Wide Telemetry Tracking: Work with business intelligence teams to build the capabilities to track user activity  With the goal to generate insights into user activity and product value.
• Full-Stack Execution: Be a key stakeholder in the "plumbing" of the API lifecycle, including GitHub governance, and CI/CD pipelines for PyPi publishing.
• Unified API Strategy
• Technical audit: Work with stakeholders across the organization to conduct a survey of existing APIs (RPC over HTTP, JSON, XML Query, REST, WebSocket, S3, Pub-Sub, etc) across the business, to identify fragmentation, authentication gaps, and areas for consolidation. Survey peers and partners to identify best-practice in API design and user experience.
• Establish Versioning Models: Work with stakeholders to define and document the hybrid versioning model to manage API updates while ensuring stability for partners and customers.
Time Line
Major milestones for the work are split into three:

• Medium (2-3yr). Design and publish a normalized multi cloud distribution framework.

At Rolls‑Royce SMR, our mission is to deliver clean, affordable energy for all. Our Small Modular Reactor (SMR) programme is a British solution to a global energy challenge, designed to accelerate decarbonisation while supporting energy security. We are uniquely positioned to become a world leader in SMR technology and one of the UK’s most exciting green export opportunities—combining proven nuclear engineering with advanced modular manufacturing to transform how low‑carbon power is delivered.
The Team
You’ll be joining the Materials & Chemistry team. This cross‑functional group supports the entire lifecycle of the RR‑SMR—from concept design to decommissioning—providing essential expertise across Reactor Plant & Systems, Components & Mechanical Equipment, Manufacturing Engineering, the Conventional Island, and both internal and external supply chain stakeholders. Your contribution will help shape the safety, integrity, and performance of the SMR design.
Role Summary
We are recruiting a Senior Materials Engineer – Welding & Manufacturing, a key technical role responsible for developing, assuring, and integrating the welding and manufacturing requirements that underpin the RR‑SMR design. This role is essential to ensuring that all structural materials, welds, special processes, and manufacturing routes meet our expectations for nuclear‑grade integrity. You will act as a technical partner to our supply chain, and a trusted advisor within multidisciplinary engineering teams. Your contribution will significantly influence compliance, manufacturability, and long‑term plant safety.
Key Responsibilities
You will be doing…
•
Leading the development and delivery of material specifications and providing expert manufacturing support.
•
Acting as technical partner for suppliers who design and manufacture metallic components—reviewing and approving Methods of Manufacture, documentation packs, data cards, and final documentation.
•
Supporting the design and welding teams on weld consumable specification, supply, and control.
•
Conducting or supporting special process audits (such as heat treatment, forging, welding) and maintaining oversight of supplier special processes and non‑conformance resolution.
•
Collaborating closely with internal engineering and project stakeholders, representing RR‑SMR with suppliers and industry bodies.
The Impact
In this role, you will directly contribute to the integrity and manufacturability of the RR‑SMR’s key components. Your expertise ensures that welded structures, fabrication processes, and material properties meet stringent nuclear requirements. This role influences safety, schedule, supply chain readiness, and component performance—making it a high‑impact opportunity to shape how SMRs are manufactured and delivered.
Essential Qualifications & Experience
To succeed in this role, you will bring:
•
A degree (or equivalent) in a relevant engineering discipline (materials, welding, mechanical, manufacturing, etc.).
•
Strong understanding of materials systems, their behaviour, and intended nuclear uses.
•
Practical experience in materials manufacturing, including interpretation of manufacturing routes, special process controls, forging, fabrication, welding, post‑weld heat treatment, and documentation packs.
•
Experience supporting or conducting technical audits of special processes.
•
Experience working in a regulated industry, ideally nuclear or power generation. (Experience with PWR environments, ALARP/BAT, and ASME compliance beneficial.)
•
Strong communication skills and proven ability to present technical information clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Location & Working Pattern
We offer a flexible hybrid working model. This role can be based in Derby, Warrington or Manchester, with the frequency of office attendance agreed during the recruitment process based on individual and business needs.
Pay and Benefits
We anticipate paying a salary of between £50,650 - £66,500 plus:-
•
Bonus - Performance related target opportunity 12.5%
•
Benefits Allowance – £2,200 per annum, enabling you to create a bespoke package
•
Pension - 12% employer and 6% employee contributions.
•
Holidays - 28 days holiday (+ public holidays) and the ability to buy or sell up to 4 days.
•
Private Medical Insurance - BUPA single cover health care
•
Life Assurance - 6x pensionable pay
•
£250 - One-off payment for new starters for home office purchases
Why Join Us?
You’ll be joining a forward-thinking organisation that values transparency, fairness, and innovation. We offer:
•    A flexible, inclusive, and supportive working environment.
•    Opportunities for career growth in a rapidly scaling business.
•    A culture that values diversity, innovation, and continuous learning.
We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. Inclusivity is important to us, and as a Disability Confident organisation, we are committed to fair, supportive, and continually improving recruitment practices that ensure everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But we'll let you in on a secret: there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. If you feel you meet 75% of the requirements for this role, we would love to hear from you.
Also, if you are considering a career move or a sector-jump, please get in touch – we welcome applications from people with transferable skills.
Our Application Process
Due to the safety regulations within the nuclear industry, applicants will be required to participate in additional screening. These are:
•    Obtaining Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) clearance
•    Satisfactory completion of a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check

Finance is one of the most demanding and valuable environments in which to apply modern technology. You will work with complex enterprise data, mission-critical processes and high-impact decisions, using AI, data and engineering to reshape how organisations plan, control performance and allocate resources. The opportunity goes beyond building technically strong solutions: you will see how those solutions influence cash, profitability, risk and business growth, and take them from experimentation into trusted, production-ready capabilities. Working in Finance Reinvention allows you to remain close to leading-edge technology while developing an understanding of the CFO agenda, gaining exposure to senior decision-makers and building the commercial judgement needed to solve enterprise-wide challenges. This combination of deep technical capability, finance-domain expertise and measurable business impact creates a differentiated career path that is difficult to develop in a purely technology-focused role.
Purpose of the role
Core build capability for the practice. Responsible for engineering agents, the orchestration around them, the evaluation harness that establishes whether they perform, and the finance user surfaces through which they are operated. The role designs, develops, tests, deploys and operates production-grade AI applications and the services around them. Embedded within a delivery pod and working on client data from an early stage of each engagement, the role translates finance-process and control requirements into secure, observable and maintainable software.
Responsibilities
• Build and deploy agentic workflows into live finance processes, including reconciliations, journals, exception handling, disputes, collections and variance explanation, with clear acceptance criteria, human oversight and controlled failure behaviour.
• Implement LLM application patterns including tool and function calling, structured outputs, RAG or graph-based retrieval, context and memory management, multi-agent orchestration, and prompt or configuration versioning.
• Integrate with ERP and EPM systems, document repositories and workflow tooling, including the data extraction, transformation and error handling that integration requires, using secure APIs, events, identity controls and reusable connectors where appropriate.
• Write evaluations, instrument agent behaviour, and ensure failure modes are visible and recoverable, using automated functional and non-functional tests, trace-level observability, red-team scenarios and measures for quality, groundedness, latency and cost.
• Build the interfaces through which finance users review, approve, override and evidence agent actions, including provenance, citations, feedback capture, accessibility and clear error-recovery journeys.
• Package and operate solutions using cloud AI services, containers or serverless components, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, secrets and configuration management, monitoring, release controls and rollback.
• Work directly with finance users, process specialists, architects and data engineers to clarify requirements, challenge assumptions constructively, demonstrate increments and document operating procedures and runbooks.
• Contribute reusable patterns and components back to the practice asset base, including tested code, evaluation assets, reference implementations and implementation guidance.
Essential experience
• Strong software engineering discipline, including Python and at least one additional production language such as TypeScript or equivalent, version control, testing, CI, and maintainable code, together with SQL, API design, code review and secure coding practices.

• Practical experience with evaluation, observability and LLMOps or AgentOps, including versioning, monitoring, release and rollback, and analysis of quality, latency and cost.
• Understanding of secure enterprise integration and sensitive-data handling, including authentication, authorisation, secrets, logging and PII-aware design.
• Ability to work client-side and collaborate effectively with non-technical finance users, translating their needs into testable requirements while explaining options, risks and trade-offs clearly.
• At least 6 years’ relevant professional experience
Desirable
• Front-end capability alongside back-end, sufficient to deliver a usable interface independently, for example React, Next.js or an equivalent framework.
• Prior exposure to SAP, Oracle, Workday, Anaplan or OneStream, or to finance processes such as close, planning, order to cash or procure to pay.
• Experience with MCP, graph or semantic retrieval, data engineering, event-driven integration or workflow orchestration.
• Experience deploying software or data products on Azure, AWS or GCP, DataBricks, Snowflake, Palantir etc. using relevant cloud services and at least one of containers, Kubernetes or serverless patterns.
• Delivery experience in a regulated environment or under formal responsible-AI, security or model-risk controls.

Founded in 2012 by Chris Roberts, Cloud Imperium Games (CIG) is one of the largest independent game studios in the world – and home to some of the most ambitious vehicle art in the industry. We’re looking for a Vehicle Artist with hard surface modelling experience to join our team. You’ll work closely with designers, organised into strike teams, to design and build ships of all shapes and sizes – and help craft the flyable, multiplayer-ready levels players will explore.
This role calls for a strong grasp of industrial design and the technical know-how to take a concept from initial model through to a fully functioning ship in the Star Citizen universe – including the software we use and the specific functional areas (cockpits, landing gear, cargo systems, and more) that need to come together. • Collaborate with designers, technical artists, and partner studios to understand and implement correct file naming and directory structure requirements within the engine’s limitations.
• As part of a team, maintain the high standards of modelling, texturing, PBR material creation, and manufacturer design cues to provide consistent and high-quality models.

What do we expect from our Vehicle Artists?
• Hard surface modelling experience.
• Good working knowledge of 3DS Max and Photoshop.
• An eye for detail while maintaining efficient model making.
• A keen eye for industrial design.
• Avid gamer with a love of sci-fi.

Working closely with Business Development, proposal teams, therapeutic experts and operational stakeholders, you will evaluate study viability, identify potential delivery risks and develop evidence-based country, site and recruitment strategies.

You will lead and contribute to strategic feasibility activities supporting global proposals and sponsor opportunities, including:
•
Developing evidence-based feasibility strategies during the pre-award/RFP stage for global clinical trials.
•
Assessing protocol and study viability using internal performance data, external intelligence, epidemiology, patient population data and country/site insights.
•
Translating feasibility data into clear country, site and patient recruitment recommendations.
•
Identifying potential operational and recruitment risks and developing alternative scenarios and mitigation strategies.
•
Providing strategic feasibility input to Business Development and proposal teams, helping shape competitive and operationally realistic study solutions.

Partnering with therapeutic, Site Identification, Study Start-Up, Patient Recruitment & Retention and other subject-matter experts to build integrated study strategies.

Supporting the development of proposal assumptions and operational strategy.

Preparing for and participating in Bid Defense meetings, presenting feasibility strategy and recommendations directly to sponsors.
•
Acting as a feasibility subject-matter expert during sponsor discussions and strategic partnership opportunities.
•
Ensuring that feasibility assumptions, intelligence, risks and strategies are effectively transitioned to Site Identification and operational teams following study award.
•
Leading selected standalone feasibility projects and providing expert feasibility support to project teams, including rescue or change-in-scope situations.
•
Supporting and guiding less experienced feasibility colleagues and contributing to continuous improvement of feasibility processes and approaches.
What you need
We are particularly interested in candidates who bring:
•
At least 3 years of relevant experience within clinical research/drug development.
•
At least 2 years of hands-on strategic feasibility experience, including pre-award feasibility for global clinical studies.
•
Strong experience analysing and interpreting feasibility data to develop country, site and recruitment strategies.
•
Understanding of the RFP/proposal process within a CRO, pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment.

Experience assessing study viability, operational risks, patient populations and country/site potential.
•
Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn complex data into practical recommendations and compelling study strategies.
•
Confidence working cross-functionally with Business Development, clinical operations and other subject-matter experts.
•
Strong communication and presentation skills; experience supporting sponsor meetings or Bid Defense activities would be highly valuable.

Ability to operate strategically while managing multiple global opportunities and priorities.
